title: EAGER: Two-Stream Generative Recommender with Behavior-Semantic Collaboration

problem.claim: Generative sequential recommendation frames candidate item retrieval as autoregressive sequence generation.

gap.claim: Existing generative methods typically focus on either behavioral or semantic item information, neglecting their complementary nature.

contributions.claim: EAGER integrates behavioral and semantic information in a generative recommendation framework.
A two-stream generation architecture uses a shared encoder, separate behavior and semantic decoders, and confidence-based ranking.
Global contrastive learning with summary tokens supports discriminative decoding, while semantic-guided transfer promotes cross-interactions through reconstruction and estimation objectives.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe EAGER as a novel generative recommendation framework.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report superior performance over existing methods on four public benchmarks.
The authors report that source code will be publicly available on PapersWithCode.com.

narrative_sequence.summary: Generative retrieval frames sequential recommendation retrieval as autoregressive generation.
Existing methods underuse the complementarity of behavioral and semantic information.
EAGER addresses the gap with a two-stream architecture, contrastive learning, and semantic-guided transfer.
The authors report superior performance on four public benchmarks.
The authors state that source code will be publicly available.

source_observation.claim: Behavioral and semantic item information are described as complementary, but existing methods typically emphasize only one.

interpretation.claim: Recommendation systems may benefit from explicitly modeling complementary information types rather than selecting one representation.

application.claim: When multiple information types contribute to retrieval, consider separate modeling paths with mechanisms for controlled interaction.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that combining information types helps across domains or datasets beyond the reported benchmarks.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the benchmark datasets, metrics, baselines, or numerical results.
The abstract does not provide implementation details or full experimental conditions.
